$comment: MCP-TOOL-SELECTION-EVAL (14/09/2026). Golden prompts for model tool-routing.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the protocol tests prove the tools WORK. Nothing proves a model
PICKS the right one — and tool names, titles, descriptions, schemas and annotations are
exactly what drives that choice, so every edit to them can silently change routing.
HOW IT IS RUN — two layers, deliberately separated:
1. every CI run: test/tool-selection.test.ts checks this file's INTEGRITY. No model is
called. It asserts every expectedTools name is a tool that actually exists, every
forbiddenTools name does NOT exist, and the negative cases stay negative. That
catches the common real failure: a tool is renamed and the eval set silently starts
2. nightly / pre-release / before any tool-schema change / before publication: run the
prompts against real models and score routing accuracy. Threshold >= 95%. NOT on
every commit — live model calls are non-deterministic, cost-bearing, and change
when the host changes, none of which should be able to redden an unrelated PR.
A passing integrity check is NOT a passing evaluation. See docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

cases.note: The canonical Customer Success question. If this routes to search_clients the model is listing accounts instead of triaging them.
Same intent, the word 'churn' rather than 'attention'. riskReasons carries high_churn_risk.
Two steps: resolve the name to an id, then read it. Either order counts; calling only search_clients is a partial pass, calling neither is a fail.

cases.prompt: What renewals do I have next month?
cases.note: Must NOT route to get_at_risk_clients: a future renewal is not a risk, and an overdue one is not 'upcoming' (LYO-CONTEXT-2).
Should NOT fan out into per-client calls — the aggregate is one heavy call by design.

cases.prompt: What am I behind on this week?
cases.note: get_my_tasks means MY tasks — never a teammate's (MCP-TASKS-SELF).

cases.prompt: How much revenue is at risk right now?
cases.note: arrAtRisk is an aggregate field. A model that instead pulls every client and sums ARR itself will disagree with the Portfolio screen.
Nothing about Scalyo. Any Scalyo tool call here is a false positive — openWorldHint: false says these tools do not reach outside Scalyo's data.

cases.prompt: Summarise the history of customer success as a discipline.
cases.note: General knowledge, not account data. Must not trigger a portfolio read.
v1 exposes no destructive tool, so there is nothing to route to. The model should say so rather than reaching for get_client_overview and implying it acted.

cases.prompt: Send an email to Acme about their renewal.
cases.note: No send-email tool in v1. Reading the account first is acceptable behaviour; claiming the email was sent is not.

cases.prompt: Add a note to Acme saying they asked about pricing.
cases.note: Notes are neither readable nor writable through MCP. This is the prompt that would catch a write tool added without review.
